# GitHub Secrets Configuration Guide\n\nThis guide explains how to configure secrets for the Finance PWA CI/CD pipeline.\n\n## How to Add Secrets\n\n1. Go to your repository on GitHub\n2. Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions\n3. Click \"New repository secret\"\n4. Add each secret below\n\n## Required Secrets\n\n### Docker Hub (for pushing images)\n\n```\nName: DOCKER_USERNAME\nValue: your_docker_hub_username\n```\n\n```\nName: DOCKER_PASSWORD\nValue: your_docker_hub_access_token\n```\n\n### Production Deployment\n\n```\nName: DEPLOY_HOST\nValue: your.server.com\n```\n\n```\nName: DEPLOY_USER\nValue: deploy_user\n```\n\n```\nName: DEPLOY_KEY\nValue: (Your private SSH key - see below)\n```\n\n#### How to Create SSH Key for Deployment\n\n```bash\n# Generate SSH key pair\nssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f deploy_key -N \"\"\n\n# This creates:\n# - deploy_key (private key - use for DEPLOY_KEY)\n# - deploy_key.pub (public key - copy to server)\n\n# Copy public key to server\nssh-copy-id -i deploy_key.pub deploy_user@your.server.com\n\n# Add private key content to GitHub secret\ncat deploy_key | pbcopy  # macOS\ncat deploy_key | xclip   # Linux\n```\n\n### Slack Notifications (optional)\n\n```\nName: SLACK_WEBHOOK\nValue: https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL\n```\n\n#### How to Create Slack Webhook\n\n1. Go to [Slack Apps](https://api.slack.com/apps)\n2. Create New App → From scratch\n3. Name: \"Finance PWA Bot\"\n4. Select your workspace\n5. Features → Incoming Webhooks → Add New Webhook to Workspace\n6. Select channel for notifications\n7. Copy the Webhook URL\n\n### SonarCloud (for code quality)\n\n```\nName: SONAR_TOKEN\nValue: your_sonar_token\n```\n\n#### How to Create SonarCloud Token\n\n1. Go to [SonarCloud](https://sonarcloud.io)\n2. Sign up with GitHub\n3. Account → Security → Generate Token\n4. Copy token\n\n## Optional Secrets\n\n### Email Notifications\n\n```\nName: EMAIL_SERVICE_KEY\nValue: your_email_service_api_key\n```\n\n### API Keys\n\n```\nName: PLAID_CLIENT_ID\nValue: your_plaid_client_id\n```\n\n```\nName: PLAID_SECRET\nValue: your_plaid_secret\n```\n\n## Using Secrets in Workflows\n\nSecrets are accessed using `${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}`:\n\n```yaml\n- name: Deploy\n  env:\n    SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}\n    HOST: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}\n  run: |\n    echo \"$SSH_KEY\" > key\n    ssh -i key user@$HOST\n```\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n✅ **DO:**\n- Rotate secrets regularly\n- Use separate secrets for dev/prod\n- Use organization-level secrets for shared values\n- Enable secret scanning\n- Review secret access logs\n\n❌ **DON'T:**\n- Commit secrets to repository\n- Use placeholder values in code\n- Share secrets in logs or emails\n- Use the same secret across environments\n- Hardcode sensitive data\n\n## Verify Secrets Are Set\n\nCheck if secrets are properly configured:\n\n```bash\n# List all secrets (shows only names, not values)\ngh secret list\n\n# Remove a secret\ngh secret delete SECRET_NAME\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Secret not working in workflow\n\n1. Verify secret name matches exactly (case-sensitive)\n2. Check secret value doesn't have extra spaces\n3. Ensure secret is in correct repository (not organization)\n4. Re-enter secret if recently changed\n\n### Workflow can't authenticate\n\n1. Verify DEPLOY_KEY is the private key (not public)\n2. Check server's authorized_keys has public key\n3. Ensure SSH key permissions are correct (600)\n4. Test connection manually: `ssh -i key user@host`\n\n## Next Steps\n\n1. Add all required secrets\n2. Push to main branch to trigger CI/CD\n3. Check Actions tab for workflow results\n4. Fix any failures\n5. Monitor deployments\n"
